lesson.title: Pieces and cutouts

lead.text: Many shapes are rectangles joined together, or a rectangle with a corner missing. There are two ways in.
Add the areas of pieces that fit together without overlapping. Or work out the whole rectangle and subtract the missing part.
Either way, every part of the shape is counted exactly once.

steps.headline: Split a shape into pieces, or take a cutout from a bigger rectangle.

lead.text: This L-shaped floor fits inside a 9 m by 7 m rectangle. The missing corner is 3 m by 2 m.

reveal.text: You took the missing corner from the whole rectangle. What remains is the floor.

steps.headline: A floor is a 5 m by 4 m rectangle with a 3 m by 2 m rectangle joined to it. Find its area.

workedSteps.text: Add them. The pieces do not overlap.

steps.headline: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 5 cm by 3 cm corner removed. Find the area left.

workedSteps.text: Find the area of the whole rectangle.
Find the area of the cutout.

lead.text: Two rectangles are joined, edge to edge. Find the area of each, then combine them.

reveal.text: Pieces that do not overlap: add. A cutout: subtract. Both count every part once.

lead.text: A trapezoid has one pair of parallel sides, called its bases.
Flip a copy and join it to the first. The two make one parallelogram, whose base is the two bases added.

steps.headline: Two trapezoids fit together into one parallelogram.

lead.text: The parallelogram has the same height as one trapezoid. Its area is its base times the height. One trapezoid is half of it.

lesson.orientation: Calculate area by combining simple pieces or subtracting a missing corner.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: A hall is 10 m long and 6 m wide, but a 4 m by 3 m corner of it is missing, leaving an L shape.

intro.promise: By the end you'll find the area of an L shape two ways, and of a trapezoid by building a parallelogram.

recap.keyIdea: Add the areas of pieces that do not overlap, or subtract a cutout from the whole. A trapezoid is half a parallelogram.

blocks.text: You found that a 10 m by 6 m hall with a 4 m by 3 m corner missing covers 48 m².
You also found 22 m² for a patio from two pieces and 32 cm² for a trapezoid with bases 10 and 6.

recap.nextHook: A circle has no straight sides to split into rectangles. Find out what its edge and its inside need.

questions.prompt: A 9 m by 7 m floor has a 3 m by 2 m corner removed. Find the remaining area in square metres.
hints: Find the area before removing the corner.
Find the corner's area separately.
Calculate 9 × 7 − 3 × 2.
questions.onCorrect: 57 m². Whole rectangle minus the corner: 63 − 6.

misconceptions.feedback: 63 m² is the whole 9 by 7 rectangle. The corner is not part of the floor.
6 m² is the missing corner. The floor is what is left.

questions.prompt: You split a shape into two rectangles. What must be true before you add their areas?
hints: Is any part missing, or counted twice?

acceptedIdeas: They must cover the floor exactly without overlapping
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: A disjoint partition counts every part of the floor exactly once.

choices.label: They must overlap as much as possible
They must cover the floor exactly without overlapping

questions.onCorrect: The pieces must cover the shape exactly, with no overlap and no gaps, so every part is counted once.

misconceptions.feedback: Overlapping parts would be counted twice.
Perimeters don't matter when adding areas. Ask whether every part is counted exactly once.

questions.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel bases 10 cm and 6 cm, with perpendicular height 4 cm. Find its area in square centimetres.
hints: Use both parallel bases.
Average their lengths, then multiply by height.
Calculate (10 + 6) × 4 / 2.
questions.onCorrect: 32 cm². Average the bases, then multiply by the height.

misconceptions.feedback: 40 cm² is the 10 by 4 rectangle. The top base is shorter.
That is two trapezoids' worth, a parallelogram. One trapezoid is half.

questions.prompt: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 5 cm by 3 cm corner removed. Find the remaining area in square centimetres.
hints: Treat the missing part as a separate rectangle.
Subtract its area from the full rectangle.
Calculate 12 × 8 − 5 × 3.
questions.onCorrect: 81 cm². Outer rectangle minus the cutout: 96 − 15.

misconceptions.feedback: 96 cm² is the whole 12 by 8 rectangle. The cutout is not part of the shape.
15 cm² is the removed corner. Find what is left.

questions.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel bases 13 m and 7 m and perpendicular height 5 m. Find its area in square metres.
hints: Area uses the average of the two parallel bases.
Multiply that average by perpendicular height.
Calculate (13 + 7) × 5 / 2.
questions.onCorrect: 50 m². Average the two parallel bases and multiply by the height.

misconceptions.feedback: That is two trapezoids fitted into a parallelogram. One trapezoid is half.
That is 13 × 5. The top base is shorter than 13.

questions.prompt: Two area pieces overlap in a 4 m² region. Adding their areas counts that region how many times?
hints: How many of the two pieces contain the overlap?

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The overlap belongs to both pieces, so the sum counts it twice. Subtract one copy when finding their combined area.

questions.onCorrect: Twice. The overlap lies in both pieces, so adding counts it in each.

misconceptions.feedback: The overlap is inside both pieces, so it is counted at least once.
Each piece includes the overlap. How many pieces is that?

questions.prompt: What area does the floor cover, in square metres?
hints: Find the area of the full 10 m by 6 m rectangle first.
The missing corner is a smaller rectangle. What is its area?
Take the missing corner from the full rectangle.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The corner is 4 × 3 = 12. The floor is 10 × 6 − 12 = 48 m².

questions.onCorrect: 48 m². Measure the whole rectangle, then take away the part that is missing.

misconceptions.feedback: 60 m² is the full rectangle. The missing corner is not floor.
12 m² is the missing corner. The floor is what is left.

questions.prompt: A patio is a 6 m by 2 m rectangle with a 2 m by 5 m rectangle joined below it. They do not overlap. What is its area, in square metres?
hints: Find the area of each rectangle.
Do the pieces overlap?
Add the two areas.
questions.onCorrect: 22 m². The pieces do not overlap, so their areas simply add.

misconceptions.feedback: 12 m² is the top piece only. Add the lower piece too.
That adds the sides. Find each piece's area, then add the areas.

questions.prompt: A 15 m by 10 m field has a pond in one corner that measures 6 m by 5 m. What area is left for grass, in square metres?
hints: Find the area of the whole field.
Find the area of the pond.
Take the pond from the field.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The pond is 6 × 5 = 30. The grass is 15 × 10 − 30 = 120 m².

questions.onCorrect: 120 m². The grass is the whole field minus the cutout.

misconceptions.feedback: 150 m² is the whole field. The pond is not grass.
30 m² is the pond. The grass is the rest.

questions.prompt: A floor is a rectangle with a corner missing. Which finds its area?
hints: Is the missing corner part of the floor?

acceptedIdeas: The whole rectangle's area minus the missing corner's area
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: The whole rectangle's area minus the missing corner's area

choices.label: The whole rectangle's area minus the missing corner's area
The whole rectangle's area plus the missing corner's area

questions.onCorrect: Take the missing corner's area from the whole rectangle's area.

misconceptions.feedback: Adding the corner would count floor that isn't there.
Adding sides gives a distance round, not an area.

questions.prompt: Two copies of a trapezoid make one parallelogram. How does one trapezoid's area compare with the parallelogram's?
hints: How many trapezoids make the parallelogram?
questions.onCorrect: One trapezoid is half the parallelogram, because two copies make the whole.

misconceptions.feedback: Two trapezoids make the parallelogram, so each one is only part of it.
One trapezoid is only a part of the parallelogram, so it cannot be bigger.
